generation.target: time-indexed synthetic production-line states, events and policy interaction trajectories

claims.paraphrase: The framework treats station technology as a black box and explicitly does not model physical relations or monitor physical process parameters. Shifted exponential processing times, FIFO buffers, capacities, workers and routing produce a discrete-event operational simulator with dataframe-accessible state histories.

Adhesive-like assembly expiry, bounded buffers, fixed worker pools and delayed observations are meaningful operational constraints. They do not by themselves validate chemical adhesion, material mechanics or process conservation laws.

The evaluation objective is cost-weighted OK production minus scrap costs normalized by time. Per-step rewards are differences in this objective over fixed decision intervals. Fixed Tsim is chosen to represent a shift; simulated reward is not measured plant profit.

Waiting-time, part-distribution and worker-assignment cases have analytical/statistical references under stated assumptions. Worker assignments found by GEKKO are compared with LineFlow enumerations. This is operational-model verification, separate from physical-process verification.

WTJ ideal expected production is not attainable immediately after a hidden processing-time jump because observations lag. The reported WTJ optimal reference uses a tested rolling-mean agent with look-back l=1, rather than a proven global optimum over all partially observed policies.

The authors test PPO, recurrent PPO, A2C and TRPO using three seeds; Table 1 selects best hyperparameters and separates average from parenthesized maximum reward. Appendix C specifies 22 configurations and 66 trained models per scenario. Evaluations use separate simulated environments, not a factory holdout.

Policies trained from scratch converge to production-stopping deadlock with zero reward. Curriculum and memory improve learning, yet the best learned complex-line policies remain below the manually tuned heuristic reward254.6±1.1. Frequent worker reallocation can add overhead and oscillation.

Reported training times per model are about2h for WT,7h for WTJ and14h for PD5. Complex-line stacked/recurrent PPO use H100 GPUs and take roughly20h/almost6days respectively. These are training-time reports, not measured local simulation generation throughput.

The authors reconstruct a Bosch public production dataset layout with two parallel12-station pre-assembly lines and a shared subsequent line, analyzing the higher-volume pre-assembly. Limited timestamp resolution leads to nonoverlapping averages over100 consecutive parts. The reconstructed simulation is compared with actual cumulative production.

Unknown buffer slots/traversal times and assumed round-robin routing limit the real-data reconstruction. Traversal times are assumed negligible; Figure23 visually compares cumulative sink output. The PDF does not establish a separate temporal/site holdout, quantitative error bound or real-line deployment trial.

For c=0.3, exp(-c) retains about74% of the deterministic processing-time term; the prose says reduced by74%. Appendix A agent snippet visibly lacks a comma after Switch. Equation6 omits differing stochastic multipliers from the general preceding expression. Preserve these as scope/convention/snippet questions for pinned code review, not demonstrated repository bugs.

Synthetic operational data generation and actual-manufacturing offline comparison justify supporting-context retention pending adjudication. C0/V0 refer to missing governing physical coupling/verification, while M2 acknowledges Bosch real-data evaluation. Analytic operational references and real throughput evidence are retained in separate fields rather than erased or promoted to physical/industrial qualification.

generation.target: synthetic continuous process-state/action/reward trajectories for biochemical manufacturing control

claims.paraphrase: SMPL provides BeerFMT, Reactor, Atropine, PenSim and mAb simulation environments using published first-principles or empirical ODE models. States/actions represent manufacturing process variables, continuous flows and setpoints; dataset wrappers support offline control learning.

The authors report using industrial data and domain experts to validate models and tune parameters. The reviewed main PDF supplies a calibration claim, but does not provide inspectable calibration records, a quantified physical constraint metric or independent solver/metrology comparison. C1 is supported; a main-PDF-only V0 claim classification is proposed for adjudication.

The CSTR assumes a well-mixed single irreversible exothermic reaction with negligible surrounding heat loss. Phenomenological models can distort outside reliable regions; realistic non-Gaussian variability, expensive state observations and full state/action-change constraints remain incomplete.

Reported efficiency/productivity are aggregated reward comparisons. Stability denotes reward dispersion, explicitly not control-theory stability. Low variance in failed or zero-yield trajectories is not an industrial safety/stability certificate.

Offline datasets are generated by expert controllers in simulations:125000Reactor MPC,10000Atropine MPC,1000PenSim BO and1000mAb MPC trajectories. BeerFMT has a fixed-start canonical formula and no offline dataset in this report. D4RL/Torch formatting does not turn these into observed plant records.

Offline models train500epochs and online models2million environment steps. A trajectory fails on early simulator errors or action/observation limit violations and receives a large negative reward. This benchmark completion rule is separate from sensor accuracy, real safety limits and process qualification.

Atropine PLAS mean reward-4.8416 versus MPC-20.6094 is a simulated improvement. PenSim GPEI3.3071 exceeds displayed offline RL values, and mAb AWAC1374.2244 exceeds MPC1322.5012 with smaller reward dispersion. The conclusion identifies substantial gains mainly for atropine; no uniformly better industrial control follows.

PenSim prose calls PLAS the highest-average offline algorithm, but displayed means include PLAS2.0421, PLASWithPert3.0056 and COMBO3.1368. Preserve table/text separately. Reactor MPC Table1 dataset reward-3.7528 differs from Table2 evaluation-0.1912; these are different reporting contexts, not silently a common baseline.

The authors observe exploration can exploit/break simulations outside reliable regions. Reward penalties and limited input bounds do not establish a complete safety envelope or independent qualification for physical deployment.

The official-source acquired main file ends at14 reference pages and points to separate AppendixA for detailed models. Its first-page preprint footer is retained as a version question, not proof of rejection. Full main reading does not establish full supplemental coverage or publication-version adjudication.
